steps.observation:
Exit Code: 0 Duration: 601ms [stdout]

Tate watches herself in The Wrecking Crew at a local film theater. Cliff gives hitchhiker Pussycat a ride to Spahn Ranch, a former Western film set where Cliff did stunt work.

Cliff checks on George Spahn, the ranch's nearly blind owner, seeking to make sure the hippies living there are not exploiting him. Cliff physically forces ranch hippie Clem to change his car tire after Clem knifes it.

While filming an episode for the TV series Lancer, Rick struggles to deliver his lines, causing him to have an emotional breakdown in his trailer. He later gives a powerful performance during his character's speech, impressing director Sam Wanamaker and his co-star Trudi, boosting his confidence.

Schwarz books Rick to star in a Sergio Corbucci spaghetti Western. Cliff accompanies Rick for the six-month shoot in Italy, where Rick films three additional films and marries Italian starlet Francesca Capucci. Before returning to the US, a troubled Rick tells Cliff that he can no longer afford his salary, which Cliff amicably understands.

Returning to Los Angeles on August 8, 1969, Rick and Cliff go drinking. Returning to Rick's house, Cliff smokes an LSD-laced cigarette and takes his dog Brandy for a walk. Charlie Manson's followers Tex, Sadie, Katie and Flowerchild arrive to murder the Tate house occupants. Hearing a car's loud muffler, an enraged Rick orders the group off the private street. Recognizing him, the family members decide to kill him first.

--

After the police have taken statements and an ambulance takes Cliff to the hospital, Sebring and Tate invite Rick to Tate's house for a drink.

Cast

[edit]
  • Leonardo DiCaprio as Rick Dalton
  • Brad Pitt as Cliff Booth
  • Margot Robbie as Sharon Tate
  • Emile Hirsch as Jay Sebring
  • Margaret Qualley as "Pussycat"
  • Timothy Olyphant as James Stacy
  • Julia Butters as Trudi Fraser
  • Austin Butler as "Tex"
  • Dakota Fanning as "Squeaky"
  • Bruce Dern as George Spahn
  • Mike Moh as Bruce Lee
  • Luke Perry as Wayne Maunder
    • --
    "Cliff Booth" redirects here. For the upcoming sequel film, see The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.
    • Booth, Dalton's stunt double, personal assistant and best friend, is an indestructible World War II hero, specializing in knives and close-quarters combat, and "one of the deadliest guys alive."[38][39] He is a two-time Medal of Honor recipient, and has killed more Japanese soldiers than any other American soldier.[40] Booth first met Dalton during the third season of Bounty Law in 1961 when he was brought in as his stunt double. A month into the job he saved Dalton's life after he caught on fire while filming an episode.[24]: 48–50  Quentin Tarantino and Brad Pitt modeled Booth after Tom Laughlin's portrayal of Billy Jack.[41] Booth had performed stunts on The Born Losers and was paid with the denim outfit worn by Laughlin as Billy Jack, which is what he wears in the film.[24]: 25–26  Booth is inspired by Gary Kent, a stuntman for a film made at the Spahn Ranch while the Manson Family lived there,[42] as well as stuntman, professional wrestler and two-time national judo champion Gene LeBell. LeBell came to work on The Green Hornet after complaints that Bruce Lee was "kicking the shit out of the stuntmen",[43] though some aspects of LeBell's story have been disputed.[44] Like Booth, LeBell was suspected of murder but never convicted.[45] Pitt channeled Steve McQueen's stunt double Bud Ekins for his portrayal of Booth.[46] Tarantino also revealed that Booth was inspired by a real stuntman who "was the closest equivalent to Stuntman Mike" (Kurt Russell) from Death Proof. He was "absolutely indestructible... scared everybody... [and] killed his wife on a boat and got away with it."[47]
    • Billie Booth is Cliff's wife, whose death in the film—and the ambiguity surrounding it—is a reference to Natalie Wood's,[48] as is Billie's sister's name, Natalie.[49] Unlike the ambiguity of the film, in the novelization Cliff did in fact murder Billie.[50][51] He shot her with a speargun, almost tearing her in half, which he immediately regretted.[40] There is a connection between Cliff and Robert Blake, to whom Tarantino dedicates the Once Upon a Time in Hollywood novel.[52] Also in the novelization, Cliff had murdered three other people, including another stuntman.[24]: 72–73, 268 

Other fictional characters

[edit]
  • Trudi Fraser (Julia Butters), the precocious child actor who portrays Mirabella on Lancer, is inspired by Jodie Foster,[53]: 1:20:00–1:22:00  while Mirabella is inspired by the character Teresa O'Brien from said series, portrayed by Elizabeth Baur. The character is older in the real-life Lancer.[54][55] Fraser goes on to become an Academy Award–nominated actress. Her third nomination is for Tarantino's 1999 remake of The Lady in Red.[24]: 353–54 
  • Marvin Schwarz of the William Morris Agency[24]: page1  is Dalton's agent, a role that Tarantino wrote specifically for Al Pacino.[56]
  • Francesca Capucci the Italian starlet who marries Dalton is based on 1960s Italian actresses and sex symbols, namely Sophia Loren, Claudia Cardinale, Virna Lisi and Monica Vitti.[57]
